description: Every token a Rally theme may set. A theme file supplies values for these paths and no others.

groups.ref.color.neutral: The neutral ramp, ordered by contrast against the surface rather than by lightness, so a step means the same thing whichever way round a theme runs. Fills at the faint end, text at the strong end.
groups.ref.color.line: The line ramp. Borders are not faint fills: a theme that draws with space needs to flatten its lines without erasing the fills that share a contrast level with them.
groups.sys.backdrop: The window's backdrop: one painted layer behind every pane, so a theme's light runs unbroken beneath a translucent sidebar and the feed beside it rather than being repainted per pane and showing a seam at the join. Each token is a CSS `background-*` longhand under its own name, so a theme declares a backdrop the way a stylesheet would and the browser's own sizing, centring and tiling rules apply unchanged. `image` also accepts `{"svg": "<svg …>"}` for artwork drawn in the theme file and `{"url": "https://…"}` for one fetched over the network, and an array for layers.
groups.sys.color.surface: The named surfaces. Declared outright by each theme because their relationship inverts between light and dark — a dark theme makes a control recede by darkening it, a light theme by greying it.
groups.sys.color.border: The three borders the stylesheet names directly; each resolves to a step on the line ramp.
groups.sys.color.brand: Rally's own colour. `ink` is the brand read as a legible label or accent on an ordinary surface, which is a different question from `base`: the chartreuse is a fine fill on white and an illegible label on it. `mark` is narrower still — it is the logo, everywhere the logo is drawn. It takes only two values across every theme, the pair the brand is built on: the volt chartreuse on a dark ground, and near-black on a light one. It is not a theme's own reading of the brand, so a light theme does not get to warm it and a dark one does not get to mute it; a theme picks the side its background puts it on and nothing else.
groups.sys.color.accent: The hue for links, focus and selection.
groups.sys.color.success: Positive state. `fill` and `fill-edge` are a filled control — a switch that is on, a selected preset — which is neither the vivid hue nor the wash.
groups.sys.color.project: The fixed project icon palette. These fills are identity choices rather than theme accents, so a project keeps the same colour in every theme.
groups.sys.color.workstream: One colour per state a work stream can show a person in the sidebar and on the home screen. Every marker in the product draws from this group and nowhere else, so a state has one colour wherever it appears; which state wins when several are true at once is the client’s ordering, not the palette’s. Five of them are the run’s (`running`, `needs-input`, `completed`, `failed`, `stopped`) and three are the reader’s own (`unread`, `mentioned`, `unseen`), which is why they are one vocabulary: they compete for one dot.
groups.sys.color.scrim: What sits between a layer and what it covers.
groups.sys.color.focus: The colour of a focus indicator.
groups.sys.color.shimmer: The sweep across a loading skeleton.
groups.sys.color.syntax: Syntax highlighting. `prism-react-renderer` takes a JavaScript object rather than a class, so these reach it as `var()` inside an inline style.
groups.sys.color.person: One per participant, chosen by a hash of their id. Six is enough that a repeat is rare in a room and few enough that each stays distinguishable.
groups.sys.elevation.shadow: Depth. A theme that lifts nothing sets these to `none`.
groups.sys.focus.ring: Whole box-shadow values for a focus ring, so a theme controls its spread as well as its colour.
groups.sys.space.pane: Padding around a pane of content.
groups.sys.space.stack: Between message blocks in the feed.
groups.sys.space.group: Between one group of rows and the next.
groups.sys.font.family: The families. `ui` and `mono` are Geist, which ships inside the application as a `bundled` font source — a family the app only names is a family the platform substitutes, and weight then resolves against whatever it picked.
groups.sys.font.size: The sizes the interface sets, as against the document size a theme inherits.
groups.sys.font.weight: Weights. Only meaningful to the degree the resolved family supports them.
groups.sys.label: The four properties that decide whether a label is sentence case or letterspaced small capitals. They apply to the label over a turn in the feed as well as the one over a group of navigation rows.
groups.cmp.pane: The content pane. `background` is the fill drawn over the backdrop, so a theme that wants its backdrop to show through the feed sets it to `transparent` rather than to a colour that happens to match.
groups.cmp.sidebar: The navigation. `background` is a translucent tint, so `background-solid` exists for the narrow-width drawer, which sits over the content and cannot be see-through.
groups.cmp.marker: The mark at a row's leading edge. It is one element whose *shape* is a theme's decision and whose *colour* stays the row's state, so a theme can trade a dot for a line without the navigation losing what the dot was saying. It stretches between `inset-block` and the row, which is what lets one pair of values describe both a centred dot — `calc(50% - 3px)` — and a line that runs the height of the row.
groups.cmp.row: Inside a navigation row. `height-dense` is the floor under the rows whose height comes from their content; `height` is the floor for a single-line row. `background-hover` and `background-selected` are the fills; a theme that marks selection with the marker alone sets the latter to `transparent`.
groups.cmp.group-label: The band a group's label sits in.
groups.cmp.bubble: The fill behind a person's turn. A theme with one continuous ground can set all three to nothing and let the message sit on the page as plain text.
groups.cmp.composer: The message composer's frame. A theme builds either shape out of the same five values: a card sets a background, a border and a radius; a rule sets them to nothing and gives `rule-color` a hairline instead, so the composer reads as a line the page rests on rather than as a box floating over it. `rule-color-focus` is what that line does when the field has focus, which is the only feedback left once the border is gone. `send-background` and `send-radius` are the send control's own frame, which follows the composer: a flat composer with a raised button on it reads as two different surfaces.
groups.cmp.turn: Where a person's own turn sits. The three move together: a turn left-aligned but still capped reads as text that wraps early for no reason.
groups.cmp.feed: The reading column, and the label over a turn in it.
groups.cmp.markdown: Rendered markdown. Its colours were already tokens; its *measurements* were not, which is why Air's headings were smaller than the prose beneath them — `.markdown-body` scaled with `sys.font.size.prose` and the headings it contained stayed at a fixed 18/16/14.5/14. A theme that moves its prose size has to be able to move the scale above it, and the rhythm with it. The `article-*` values are the note detail's own scale: a note is read as a document rather than as a turn in a transcript, so its headings run larger than the feed's.
groups.cmp.tooltip: A surface that deliberately opposes the theme: light on a dark theme and dark on a light one, so it cannot be a ramp step in either.
groups.cmp.toggle: A switch. The knob is white on a grey track in a light theme, which is about two to one; the lift from `sys.elevation.shadow.sm` is what makes the off state read as a control.
groups.cmp.connector: Connector faces. Each keeps enough of the provider's own colour to be recognised at 20px, on a block the theme can still sit behind.
